sentences.text: By way of the instant applications, the appellant seeks condonation of delay of 505 days in filing the present appeal and 65 days in re-filing the present appeal.

8. The leaned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant states that the appellant herein has been in judicial custody since 06.10. 2018 and could not engage a counsel as his family was residing in Bihar.

9. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and fact that the appellant is in judicial custody throughout and did not have effective access to his family or to a counsel, the applications stand allowed.
10. Accordingly, the present applications stands disposed of.
CRL.M.A. 17128/2025 (rectification of clerical error in order dated 13.05.2025)
11. By way of the instant application, the appellant seeks rectification of clerical error in order dated 13.05.2025 and to substitute the figure 465 days with 65 days.
12. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant states that the delay in re-filing the present appeal is of 65 days.

The learned counsel for the appellant has placed on record two documents wherein the date of filing the present appeal is mentioned as 22.01.2025 and the date of re-filing the present appeal is mentioned as 25.04.2025.

She prays that the same may be corrected in order dated 13.05.2025.
13.
Ordered accordingly.

14. Para 1 of order dated 13.05.2025, be now read as under:
"1.
By way of the present applications, the applicant seeks condonation of delay of 505 days in filing the above-captioned appeal and 65 days in re filing the above-captioned appeal."

15.

By way of the present application, the applicant/appellant seeks suspension or sentence,
awarded to him vide judgment of conviction dated 09.06.2023 and order on sentence dated 04.08.2023, in CIS-SC No. 543/2018 arising out of FIR bearing no. 215/2018, registered at Police Station Moti Nagar, Delhi, for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(i)(n)/376AB/377/506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereafter 'IPC') and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act 2012 (hereafter 'POCSO Act') passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Special Court (POCSO), West District, Tis Hazari Court Complex, Delhi,

whereby the appellant was sentenced to undergo (i) rigorous imprisonment for a period of twenty years, and pay a fine of Rs.1,00,000/- for offence punishable under Section 376AB of IPC and in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one year;
(ii) rigorous imprisonment for a period of ten years, and pay a fine of Rs.50,000/- for offence punishable under Section 377 of IPC and in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six months; (iii) rigorous imprisonment for a period of two years, and pay a fine of Rs.10,000/- for offence punishable under Section 506 of IPC and in default of payment of fine, to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of one month.
All the sentences were ordered to run concurrently.
Fine has not been paid by the convict.
The benefit of Section 428 of Cr.P.C. was granted to the convict.
16. Nominal roll of the appellant has been received.
17. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant states that This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 13/08/2025 at 21:49:01 the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case on prior monetary dispute with the father of the victim, who was working in the factory of victim's father.
It is submitted that the appellant is facing trial since the year 2018 and is about 28 years of age.
It is also submitted that the appellant has been in judicial custody for about 06 years and 09 months.
He further states that the appellant is not involved in any other case and the jail record shows that his conduct is satisfactory.
Therefore, the sentence awarded to the appellant/applicant in the present case may be suspended during the pendency of the present appeal.
18. In light of the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, the present application is allowed.

It is directed that the sentence awarded to the appellant/applicant shall remain suspended during the pendency of the present appeal, subject to his furnishing a personal bond to the tune of Rs. 10,000/-
with one surety bond of the like amount, subject to satisfaction of the learned Trial Court/Successor Court/Link Court/Duty Judge concerned on the following terms and conditions:
i) The appellant/applicant shall not leave the country without prior permission of the learned Trial Court.
ii) In case of change of residential address/contact details and phone number, the applicant shall promptly inform the same to the concerned Trial Court.
19. Accordingly, the present application stands disposed of.
In view of order passed in application bearing No. CRL.M.(BAIL) 1057/2025, this application has become infructuous.
